meanings.note: Compartment of a car for luggage. Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'trunk, boot, luggage rack' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Close the trunk quickly!
Great, close the trunk quickly!

examples.text: Да, все вещи уже загрузили в багажник.
examples.trans: Yes, all things have already been loaded into the trunk.

the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.trans: Faster!
He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor

future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
At the start of a sentence. Core Russian pron meaning 'everything, all; that's it' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: That's what you said.
I speak Russian.
Well, the thing you said.

meanings.note: put items onto a vehicle or into bags

examples.trans: We are carefully loading all the money.
The workers were loading bags into the truck.

examples.text: Мы можем уже сейчас грузить сумки?
examples.trans: Can we already load the bags right now?

meanings.note: Head of a Russian region. From Latin 'gubernator' (helmsman, governor, borrowed from Greek 'kybernetes').

examples.trans: The governor has come to the town.
Does the governor support you?
And does the governor support you?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.
Quiet, stop! It really hurts!

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: I have no money.
The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'верие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'trust' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
It's a question of trust.
The meeting undermined trust in Samsonov.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I'm thinking about work.
I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.note: In court or sport. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'щита'). Common feminine noun meaning 'defence, protection' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'щита'). Common feminine noun meaning 'defence, protection' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: How are we going to build our defence?
Thank you for the protection.

examples.text: Вы под нашей защитой. Вам не о чем волноваться.
examples.trans: You are under our protection. You have nothing to worry about.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

Кажется as a parenthetical word. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to seem', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.trans: I think he's right.
I think I've seen you.
I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?
As you all know...
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Head of a government ministry. Common masculine noun meaning 'minister' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They are considering you for the post of minister.
The new minister held the first meeting.

examples.text: Тебя всерьёз рассматривают на пост министра.
examples.trans: They are seriously considering you for the post of minister.

meanings.note: Short for может быть. Core Russian part meaning 'maybe, perhaps' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Maybe you could help?
Maybe tomorrow.
I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: молодой человек = young man (polite address)

examples.text: Молодой человек, как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

examples.text: Молодой человек, а как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.trans: Never!

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.
No! Never!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ласть'). Common feminine noun meaning 'region, province, oblast' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We lifted the barbell, we'll raise the region!
The whole region knows his name.

examples.text: Подняли штангу, поднимем область! А теперь уберите эту штангу!
examples.trans: We lifted the barbell, we'll raise the region! And now remove this barbell!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('huge, enormous').

examples.trans: Our chances are huge.
Thank you so much!

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: Recover spent money. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win back, recoup', paired with 'отбивать'.

examples.text: Я быстро отобью все эти деньги.
examples.trans: I will quickly win all this money back.

examples.text: Инвестор надеется отбить вложенные средства за год.
examples.trans: The investor hopes to recoup the invested funds within a year.
Just tenderize it well first!

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Отдать + dative of the person. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give (away), to hand over', paired with 'отдавать'.

Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give (away), to hand over', paired with 'отдавать'.

examples.trans: Give me the keys.
He will hand over the money.

examples.text: Потом надо отдать москвичам твои деньги из подвала.
examples.trans: Then I have to give your money from the basement to the Moscow people.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: showing potential for future success

examples.text: Ты молодой и очень перспективный руководитель.
examples.trans: You are a young and very promising leader.

examples.text: Вы очень способный и перспективный повар.
examples.trans: You are a very capable and promising cook.

meanings.note: + instrumental (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'under' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'under' in everyday speech.
Под мою ответственность. Core Russian prep meaning 'under' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The cat is under the table.
On my responsibility.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.

meanings.note: Disappoint expectations. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'вести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to let down, fail', paired with 'подводить'.

examples.trans: I will never let you down.

examples.text: Надёжный друг никогда не подведёт в беде.
examples.trans: A reliable friend will never let you down in trouble.

examples.text: Подведём итоги твоей первой рабочей недели.
examples.trans: Let us sum up your first work week.

meanings.note: Пост мэра = the office of mayor. Common masculine noun meaning 'post, office' in everyday Russian.
Common masculine noun meaning 'post, office' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он идёт на пост мэра города.
examples.trans: He is running for the post of mayor of the city.

examples.text: Он выдвигает свою кандидатуру на пост мэра города!
examples.trans: He is putting forward his candidacy for the post of mayor of the city!

examples.text: Тебя всерьёз рассматривают на пост министра.
examples.trans: They are seriously considering you for the post of minister.

meanings.en: to bargain, haggle for a bit
meanings.note: Negotiate a price. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'торговаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bargain a little', paired with 'торговаться'.

examples.trans: Maybe it is worth bargaining a little?
The buyer decided to bargain a little at the market.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слабиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to relax', paired with 'расслабляться'.

examples.trans: Vanya, relax.
I want to relax.

examples.text: Ваня, расслабься. В этот раз без обмана.
examples.trans: Vanya, relax. This time there's no trick.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become
Решить задачу. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'head, leader, manager' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She is the new head of the headquarters.

examples.text: Я новый руководитель предвыборного штаба Павла Юрьевича.
examples.trans: I am the new head of Pavel Yuryevich's campaign headquarters.

examples.text: Здравствуйте! Я не журналистка. Я руководитель штаба Ивана Самсонова.
examples.trans: Hello! I'm not a journalist. I'm the head of Ivan Samsonov's campaign.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Серьёзно? = really?. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ерьёзно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Are you serious?
I mean it.
No way, what, seriously?

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!
Rather yes than no.
Bring the clothespin quickly!

meanings.note: Совершенно верно = quite right. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овершенно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!
Thank you for your trust!

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Сколько стоит? = how much is it?. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cost; to be worth'.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cost; to be worth'.

examples.trans: How much does it cost?
The console costs five thousand.
And how much does the console cost?

meanings.note: For carrying things. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'умка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'bag, handbag' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давайте я вам помогу с сумкой.
examples.trans: Let me help you with your bag.
She put the keys into her bag.
Take out all the large bags quickly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'умма'). Common feminine noun meaning 'sum, amount' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The sum is very large.
What amount?

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Now I'm the boss.
Now everything's fine.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.trans: I was only looking.
Just one.
I was only looking!

meanings.note: Negotiate price or conditions. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bargain, haggle', paired with 'поторговаться'.

examples.trans: They never bargain in Moscow.

examples.text: На восточном базаре принято весело торговаться.
examples.trans: It is customary to bargain merrily at an oriental bazaar.

examples.text: Аркаша, в Москве никогда не торгуются.
examples.trans: Arkasha, they never bargain in Moscow.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!

examples.trans: He is a good person.

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
